label: Algebraic Structures
notes: Open with the chapter purpose. Geometric deep learning rests on group symmetry: equivariance, invariance, and homogeneous spaces. The deck follows PDF pages 4 through 19. It covers groups, rings, fields, modules, group actions, and the equivariance vocabulary that the rest of the book uses.

label: Groups
notes: Define a group as a set with an associative binary operation, identity, and inverses. Emphasize examples relevant to GDL: rotation groups SO(d), permutation groups S_n, translation groups, and gauge groups. Subgroups, cosets, and homomorphisms are the structural tools used throughout the chapter.

label: Rings and Fields
notes: Cover rings and fields. A ring has addition and multiplication compatible by distributivity; a field is a commutative ring where every nonzero element is invertible. The reals and complex numbers are the standard fields in GDL; finite fields appear in some discrete contexts. Modules over rings generalize vector spaces.

label: Group Actions
notes: Introduce group actions. An action of G on X is a homomorphism from G to the symmetries of X. Orbits, stabilizers, and orbit-stabilizer theorem organize the action. In GDL, the data domain X carries a G-action and the learned functions are required to be equivariant under this action.

label: Equivariance
notes: Define equivariance. A function f from X to Y between G-spaces is equivariant if f composed with the action on X equals the action on Y composed with f. Invariance is the special case where the Y-action is trivial. Equivariant networks are the principal architectural device in geometric deep learning.

label: Recap
notes: Close the chapter. Groups encode symmetry, rings and fields give scalar arithmetic, group actions formalize how symmetry acts on data, and equivariance constrains what learned functions look like. The remaining chapters build geometric, analytical, and spectral machinery on top of this algebraic backbone.
